proof.text: For each i with 0≤i<r put R_i=R/(f_1,…,f_i), with R_0=R. Regularity of f says that multiplication by f_{i+1} on R_i is injective; taking its cokernel gives an exact sequence 0→R_i→R_i→R_{i+1}→0. The k-module S is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] preserves this injection after tensoring over k with S. The quotient/base-change isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] identifies the resulting map with multiplication by f_{i+1}⊗1 on T/(f_1⊗1,…,f_i⊗1). Thus every prefix multiplication in the f-block is injective.

After the f-block, write R_f=R/(f). For each 0≤j<s put S_j=S/(g_1,…,g_j). Regularity of g gives an exact sequence 0→S_j→S_j→S_{j+1}→0 whose middle map is multiplication by g_{j+1}. The k-module R_f is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] preserves the injection after tensoring with R_f. Using the canonical symmetry of tensor products and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], identify the successive quotients with R_f⊗_k S_j; the map is multiplication by 1⊗g_{j+1}. Hence every prefix multiplication in the g-block is injective.

Applying [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] first to the f-block and then to the g-block gives the canonical quotient isomorphism T/(h)≅R/(f)⊗_k S/(g), carrying a⊗b to ā⊗b̄. The two factors are nonzero by the final-quotient clause of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and the Mathlib leaf [lem-pur-field-vector-space-tensor-nontrivial] says their tensor product over k is nonzero. Together with the injections from the preceding two steps, the defining criterion [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] proves that h is regular. If r=0 or s=0, the corresponding injection list is empty and the same quotient and nonzero-factor argument applies, so the empty-sequence cases are included.

Let q be a prime of T containing the ideal generated by h. The injections established in the first two steps give the weak regularity hypotheses for the full ordered sequence h, and every entry lies in q. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] with A=T, p=q and a_i=h_i yields that h_1/1,…,h_{r+s}/1 is a regular sequence in T_q, of length r+s.

title: Tensor-product concatenation of regular sequences
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $R,S$ be commutative unital $k$-algebras, and let $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ be regular sequences in $R$ and $S$ respectively [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Thus every successive multiplication map is injective and the final quotients $R/(f)$ and $S/(g)$ are nonzero. Put $T=R\otimes_k S$ with its usual algebra tensor-product ring structure [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then the ordered tuple
$$h=(f_1\otimes1,\ldots,f_r\otimes1,1\otimes g_1,\ldots,1\otimes g_s)$$
is a regular sequence in $T$. Its quotient is canonically
$$T/(h)\cong R/(f)\otimes_k S/(g),$$
by the homomorphism $a\otimes b\mapsto\overline a\otimes\overline b$. In particular the final quotient is nonzero, and at every prime of $T$ containing $(h)$ the images in the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of $h$ remain a regular sequence of length $r+s$. The assertion includes either or both sequences being empty.
